content.title: About
content.content: Jalapeno is a small hot pepper (Capsicum annuum) cultivated mainly in Mexico and the United States. Fresh and seeded, it is bright green, crisp, and moderately spicy. The pepper is commonly used in salsas, sauces, marinades, and as a topping for many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name jalapeno comes from the Mexican city of Xalapa.
Heat is measured on the Scoville scale (SHU) ranging from 2,500 to 8,000 units.
Most capsaicin – the compound that gives heat – is concentrated in the seeds and inner membrane.
Dried jalapenos are called “chipotle” and are smoked for use in Mexican cuisine.
Jalapenos are one of the most popular fresh peppers in the United States.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: A 100‑g serving of raw jalapeno provides about 115 mg of vitamin C, supporting immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains capsaicin
items.content: Capsaicin may boost metabolism, aid fat burning, and have mild analgesic effects.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in the pepper converts to vitamin A, important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A medium jalapeno contains fewer than 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly addition.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Spicy foods can cause discomfort for people with gastritis, ulcers, or a sensitive stomach.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to nightshade family vegetables.

items.title: Heat sensitivity
items.content: Excessive consumption may lead to mouth burning and tearing.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Seeded jalapeno can be sliced and added to salads, salsas, guacamole, sandwiches, or used in marinades. It can also be lightly sautéed, roasted, or incorporated into sauces for extra heat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh jalapenos in the refrigerator in an airtight container or a bag with a small amount of moisture. Properly stored, they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Freeze sliced pieces if you plan to use them later.
